_comment: Fixed formats with filled slots, not a fresh composition each time.
Why: a model writing every email from scratch is a bet, taken again on
every send, that it lands the tone. Templates make the wording a thing you
improve once and then keep. They also cost nothing to produce — the audit
findings are already written for the owner to read, so most of these need
Slots are {braced}. Anything left unfilled is an error, never sent — see
loom/services/email_templates.py. Edit the wording freely; keep the slot
Legal note for the outreach templates: pitching work is a commercial
electronic message under the Spam Act, so sender identity and an opt-out
line are not optional. Both live in `signature` and are appended

first_contact.label: First contact
first_contact.subject: {business} — {subject_hook}
first_contact.body:
Hi,

I had a look at {business} on my phone and {problem_sentence}.

I rebuilt it as it could be — {built_from}:
{demo_url}

It's a mock-up, not a live site, and it takes me {timeline} to finish properly for {price}. One payment, no monthly fee, and you own it.

Worth a look?

first_contact_no_site.label: First contact — no website
first_contact_no_site.subject: {business} — a website, already half built
first_contact_no_site.body:
Hi,

{business} doesn't come up with a website when people search for you, so anyone deciding where to go tonight is choosing from whoever does.

I built one to show you what it could look like:
{demo_url}

The layout is real; the photos and menu are placeholders until you send me yours. Finished properly it's {price} — one payment, no monthly fee, and it's yours.

Worth a look?

follow_up.label: Follow-up (once, then stop)
follow_up.subject: Re: {business}
follow_up.body:
Hi,

Just in case my last note got buried — the mock-up I made for {business} is still up:
{demo_url}

Happy to take it down if it's not of interest; just say so and I won't write again.

quote.label: Quote after a reply
quote.subject: {business} — what's involved
quote.body:
Hi {contact_name},

Good to hear from you. Here's what I'd do:

· Build out the site you saw, with your real photos, menu and hours
· Set it up on your own domain, ready for Google
· {revisions} after it's live, so we get it right

{price} in total. One payment, nothing monthly. {timeline_capitalised} from when you send me the content.

If you'd like a booking form or online ordering as well, that's {price_with_extras} all in.

What I need from you to start: your logo if you have one, a few photos, and your menu in any form — a photo of the printed one is fine.

Happy to talk it through on the phone if that's easier.

content_request.label: Chasing content
content_request.subject: {business} — ready when you are
content_request.body:
Hi {contact_name},

Everything's set up on my end. Whenever you get a chance, send through:

· Your menu — a photo of the printed one is fine
· A few photos of the room or the food, from a phone is fine
· Your logo, if you have a file for it

I'll have the first version back to you in {timeline} of receiving them.

handover.label: Handover
handover.subject: {business} — you're live
handover.body:
Hi {contact_name},

{business} is live:
{live_url}

A few things worth knowing:

· It works on phones, tablets and desktops — have a look on yours
· Google can find it; it may take a few days to show up in search
· The domain and everything on it belongs to you

You've got {revisions} included — send me anything you want changed and I'll do it, no charge.

Thanks for the work. If it does what you wanted, a word to anyone else on the street who needs one would mean a lot.

revision_ack.body:

{change_list}

problem_phrases._note: How each audit finding reads inside a sentence, owner-facing. Falls back to the finding's own detail text. contact_mismatch is left out on purpose — its own detail names both numbers, which reads stronger than a generic clause.
problem_phrases.mobile_broken: the page runs off the side of the screen — you have to scroll sideways to read it
problem_phrases.not_mobile_ready: it comes up as a shrunken desktop page, so everything's too small to tap
problem_phrases.dead: the address on your Google listing doesn't load at all
problem_phrases.unreachable: the site wouldn't load for me
problem_phrases.timeout: it took so long to load that most people would have given up
problem_phrases.ssl_invalid: the browser blocks it with a security warning before anything shows
problem_phrases.error_page: the home page comes back with an error
problem_phrases.renders_empty: the page loads but almost nothing appears
problem_phrases.broken_images: several of the photos don't load — you just get empty boxes
problem_phrases.no_website: there's no website on your Google listing at all
problem_phrases.social_only: the only thing listed is a Facebook page
problem_phrases.placeholder: it still shows the 'coming soon' placeholder
problem_phrases.free_subdomain: it's on a free builder's address rather than your own
problem_phrases.slow: it takes a few seconds to appear, which is a long time on mobile data
problem_phrases.stale: it hasn't been touched in years — the footer still shows an old year
problem_phrases.tiny_text: the text is too small to read on a phone
problem_phrases.phone_not_tappable: your phone number is on there as plain text — on a mobile you can't tap it to call, you have to memorise it and type it back in
problem_phrases.no_link_preview: when someone shares your address on Facebook or in a WhatsApp group it comes up as an empty grey box instead of a photo of the place
problem_phrases.no_favicon: there's no little icon on the browser tab, so it shows a blank sheet of paper next to your name
problem_phrases.menu_is_a_file: your menu opens as a download rather than a page — on a phone you have to pinch and zoom to read it, and Google can't index a word of what you serve

subject_hooks._note: Subject line per finding code, keyed the same way as problem_phrases. Falls back to `default` when a code has no hook.
subject_hooks.phone_not_tappable: the phone number on your site
subject_hooks.no_link_preview: how your link looks when shared
subject_hooks.ssl_invalid: the security warning on your site
subject_hooks.no_https: the 'not secure' warning on your site
subject_hooks.slow: how long your site takes to load

source_notes._note: How the demo describes where its content came from. Chosen by whether the harvest actually produced anything: claiming a page was built from their site when their site is a 404 or a blank install is a claim the owner can disprove in one click, in the first email they get from a stranger.
source_notes.harvested: your own name and details, built from what's already on your site
source_notes.placeholder: your own name, address and hours — the photos and wording are placeholders until you send me yours
